title: Poiseuille profile
subject: physics
brief: A broad pair of engraved pipe walls frames a bow-shaped speed envelope. Nine arrows grow toward the axis; a detached circular section establishes the tube rather than a flat channel.
basis: For steady, fully developed laminar flow of an incompressible Newtonian fluid in a straight circular tube, u(r)=G(R²-r²)/(4mu), where G=-dp/dx. The drawn profile and arrow lengths follow this parabola. A hypothetical R=0.005 m, mu=0.001 Pa s, density 1000 kg/m³ and G=32 Pa/m give maximum speed 0.2 m/s, mean speed 0.1 m/s and diameter-based Reynolds number 1000.
limitations: A meridional section and separate circular-section key, with editorial wall thickness and independent display scales. Assumes no slip, a uniform circular tube and fully developed laminar flow. Entrance effects, turbulence, non-Newtonian behavior, compressibility and wall deformation are omitted. This is not a physiological or pipe-design prediction.
provenance: Original authored vector geometry. Factual source principles inform the limited model; no source figure or photograph is traced or reproduced.

title: Stokes settling
subject: physics
brief: A single engraved sphere hangs between two upward forces and one longer downward force. Three detached bars above expose the force sum; a separate descent arrow reserves the right-hand negative space.
basis: A rigid sphere at terminal speed in creeping flow has Stokes drag 6 pi mu R U. Weight minus buoyancy balances drag, so U=2(rho_p-rho_f)gR²/(9mu). The hypothetical 50-micrometre radius sphere has density 2500 kg/m³ in fluid of density 1000 kg/m³ and viscosity 0.1 Pa s. The weight, buoyancy and drag arrows have lengths in ratio 5:2:3, with the latter two opposed to weight.
limitations: Isolated spherical particle in an effectively unbounded, quiescent Newtonian fluid at terminal speed. Particle and force display scales are enlarged and independent of the velocity arrow. Surface etching is not fluid streamlines. Brownian motion, walls, other particles, non-sphericity, transient history and finite-Reynolds-number corrections are omitted.

title: Hydraulic jump
subject: physics

basis: The classical momentum balance for a horizontal rectangular hydraulic jump gives y2/y1=(sqrt(1+8 Fr1²)-1)/2. For Fr1=3 and y1=0.08 m, the depth ratio is about 3.772. The two remote water depths use this ratio, and the downstream mean-speed arrows are shortened by its reciprocal to conserve discharge per unit width. The modeled downstream Froude number is below one.

The curved jump surface, recirculation arc and sparse air marks are qualitative, not computed turbulence, bubble trajectories or a measured jump length. title: Rankine vortex
subject: physics
brief: Broken circular streamlines wrap an off-center core, leaving a clean lower-right sector. Five tangential arrows rise and then shorten; a detached kinked profile contrasts solid-body rotation with inverse-radius decay.
basis: The ideal Rankine vortex has tangential speed v=Omega r within core radius a and v=Omega a²/r outside it. limitations: An ideal inviscid two-dimensional vortex, not a viscously evolving flow, tornado forecast or draining bathtub. Streamline arcs are selected portions of circles and do not show inward spiraling. The core boundary is a vorticity interface, not a solid wall.
